covers: INT 16h, the keyboard BIOS: every function and subfunction the emulator's INT16_Handler has a case for.

entries.name: get keystroke
entries.description: Waits for a key and removes it from the keyboard buffer, returning its scan code and ASCII code.
entries.behaviour: AH = scan code, AL = ASCII. Enhanced keys (scan code above 84h, or low byte F0h) are removed and skipped, and E0h-prefixed keypad Enter and / become scan codes 1Ch and 35h. With no key it advances IP into an idle loop, repeating the call; IRQ 1 is first unmasked unless 'unmask keyboard on int 16 read' is off.

entries.name: get enhanced keystroke
entries.description: Waits for a key, enhanced keys included, and removes it from the keyboard buffer.
entries.behaviour: AH = scan code, AL = ASCII, with no skipping or keypad translation; a key with low byte F0h and a non-zero high byte returns with AL cleared. With no key it advances IP into an idle loop so the call repeats, after unmasking IRQ 1 as AH=00h does.

entries.name: check for keystroke
entries.description: Reports whether a key is waiting in the keyboard buffer without removing it.
entries.behaviour: A waiting non-enhanced key gives ZF clear and AX = the key; enhanced keys at the head are removed and skipped; with no key ZF is set. Unless 'int16 keyboard polling undocumented cf behavior' is off, CF is also set with a key and clear without one; IF is set on return.
entries.differs: The list leaves CF undefined; by default the emulator sets CF when a key is waiting and clears it when not.

entries.name: check enhanced keystroke
entries.description: Reports whether a key, enhanced keys included, is waiting in the keyboard buffer without removing it.
entries.behaviour: No key gives ZF set and AX unchanged; a key gives ZF clear and AX = the key, AL cleared when the low byte is F0h and the high byte is not zero, and nothing is skipped. Ctrl+Break stores 0000h, so AX=0 with ZF clear is possible. CF is not touched and IF is set on return.

entries.name: get shift flags
entries.description: Returns the keyboard shift flags.
entries.behaviour: AL = the BIOS data area byte at 0040:0017 (bit 7 Insert, 6 Caps Lock, 5 Num Lock, 4 Scroll Lock, 3 Alt, 2 Ctrl, 1 left Shift, 0 right Shift). AH is not changed.

entries.name: set typematic rate
entries.description: Sets the keyboard typematic delay and repeat rate.
entries.behaviour: AL=00h writes F3h then 20h to port 60h (500 ms delay, 30 characters per second); AL=05h writes F3h then (BH AND 3) shifted left 5, OR (BL AND 1Fh). Any other AL is logged as unhandled and does nothing; AH is not changed.
entries.differs: The list also defines AL=01h to 04h and 06h (read back rate and delay); the emulator does nothing for them.

entries.name: store keystroke
entries.description: Stores the key in CX in the keyboard buffer.
entries.behaviour: CX is the key (CH scan code, CL ASCII); AL=00h if stored, 01h if the buffer is full, and 00h without storing while the Pause flag (bit 3 at 0040:0018) is set. CGA, PCjr, Olivetti and 3270 PC machines use a fixed buffer at 1Eh to 3Eh; PC-98 uses its own at 0502h.

entries.name: get extended shift
entries.description: Returns the extended keyboard shift flags.
entries.behaviour: AL = the byte at 0040:0017 as for AH=02h. AH = bits 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 of the byte at 0040:0018 (left Ctrl, left Alt, Scroll, Num and Caps Lock pressed), bit 7 = its bit 2 (SysReq), and bits 2 and 3 of the byte at 0040:0096 (right Ctrl, right Alt).

entries.name: dbcs shift control
entries.description: Sets or gets the DOS/V double-byte shift status held by the front-end processor.
entries.behaviour: Acts only on a DOS/V CJK machine with the front-end processor input-assist flag set, and only in Windows and macOS builds; otherwise it does nothing. AL=00h: DL bits 0 or 7 on enables the host IME, else disables it. AL=01h: DL = 81h if it is enabled, else 00h.
entries.differs: The list sets and returns a DX shift-status word; the emulator uses only DL as an IME on/off switch and flag.

entries.name: shift display control
entries.description: Enables, disables or queries the display of the DOS/V shift status row.
entries.behaviour: Acts only on a DOS/V CJK machine with the front-end processor input-assist flag set; otherwise it does nothing. AL=00h or 01h stores AL in a variable (initially 01h), AL=02h returns it in AL.

entries.name: ax keyboard country
entries.description: Sets or gets the keyboard country mode of an AX machine.
entries.behaviour: Acts only on a JEGA (AX) machine; elsewhere it returns with registers unchanged. AL selects the subfunction, 00h set or 01h get; any other AL is logged and returns AL=02h.

entries.name: set kbd country
entries.description: Sets the AX keyboard BIOS country mode.
entries.behaviour: BX = 0001h (US) or 0051h (Japan), applied by setting or clearing bit 6 of the AX status byte; AL=00h on success and AL=01h for any other BX. On a machine that is not JEGA it does nothing and AL is unchanged.

entries.name: get kbd country
entries.description: Gets the AX keyboard BIOS country mode.
entries.behaviour: BX = 0051h if bit 6 of the AX status byte is set, else 0001h, and AL=00h. On a machine that is not JEGA it does nothing and BX and AL are unchanged.

entries.name: ax read shift status
entries.description: Reads the shift key states and the Kana lock of an AX machine.
entries.behaviour: Only on a JEGA machine in Japanese keyboard mode (otherwise registers are unchanged): AL = the byte at 0040:0017 and AH = the Kana lock bit, 02h when locked and 00h when not.
entries.differs: The list gives AH=01h for Kana lock on; the emulator returns 02h.

entries.name: word tsr check
entries.description: Answers the Microsoft Word keyboard TSR cooperation call.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs it as a Word TSR compatible call and returns with registers unchanged, so AX is not set to 4D53h, the answer the list gives for a present keyboard TSR; Word then installs its own handlers.

entries.name: j3100 set key data
entries.description: A J-3100 keyboard BIOS call that stores the key in BX in the keyboard buffer.
entries.behaviour: Only on a J-3100 machine in its Japanese video mode (74h); elsewhere nothing happens. BX is the key; AX=0000h if stored, AX=FFFFh if the buffer is full. The store follows the AH=05h rules.

entries.name: j3100 check key buffer
entries.description: A J-3100 keyboard BIOS call that counts the keys in the keyboard buffer.
entries.behaviour: Only on a J-3100 machine in its Japanese video mode (74h); elsewhere nothing happens. AX = the number of keys waiting, or FFFFh when that equals the buffer size in words; BX = the machine code of the emulated J-3100 model.
